title: openai/chat.completions parity: streaming stability, roles, stop/logprobs, and response formatting
author: Ethan Cole
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with common OpenAI behavior, focusing on streaming stability, correct handling of roles, deterministic stop sequence behavior, streaming logprobs, and response formatting/structured output. This PR unifies request parameter parsing, stabilizes the streaming adapter (backpressure and partial events), and implements logprobs/stop semantics that match downstream expectations.

Scope and summary: single changeset that touches the compatibility layer, streaming runtime adapter, SDK shims, docs, and tests. Key areas: role normalization (system/user/assistant), stop sequence enforcement for both buffered and streaming modes, emission of incremental logprobs in streaming events, consistent response-formatting for structured output (content-type / parse hints), and additional e2e tests for streaming edge cases.

Highlights: 
- Streaming stability: improved chunking and flow-control in streaming_adapter.go to avoid stuck streams under heavy concurrency; added keepalive and explicit end-of-stream events for OpenAI-style clients.
- Roles: normalize role names and tolerate legacy keys (e.g., "assistant" vs "assistant_label"). Ensure system messages are preserved and prioritized in prefix caching.
- Stop sequences: implement deterministic early-stop in streaming by scanning incoming tokens and emitting a final event that includes any trailing token fragments per OpenAI behavior.
- Logprobs: support streaming logprobs events (partial token scores) and an aggregated final logprobs object on completion; added deterministic rounding and token-index alignment to match OpenAI's indices.
- Response formatting: add heuristics and explicit hints for structured outputs (json_schema/response_format) so SDKs can surface parsing helpers; update docs with examples.

Testing and validation: Added unit and e2e tests (tests/e2e/openai_streaming.test.ts, tests/unit/openai_compat_test.go) that cover: multiple stop sequences, concurrent streaming clients, logprob alignment, function/tool calling handoff in streaming mode, and fallbacks when streaming fails (graceful degradation to non-streaming response). CI passes after one flake fix. Benchmarks show negligible latency regressions and improved tail latency for heavy streaming workloads.

Backward compatibility and migration: The OpenAI compatibility layer keeps the existing Redwood API unchanged; new behavior is opt-out only via explicit compatibility flags. No breaking changes expected by default.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement role normalization and system-message priority
- [x] Streaming adapter flow control + end-of-stream semantics
- [x] Streaming logprobs events + final aggregated logprobs
- [x] Deterministic stop sequence handling in streaming and buffered modes
- [x] SDK shims (python/ts) for response formatting helpers
- [x] Docs and example updates
- [x] Tests and CI green

Related: ENG-8241 (parity request), ENG-8312 (streaming stability), existing PRs pr-25678/pr-24801 which incrementally introduced streaming function calls and roles handling.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the streaming_adapter.go backpressure strategy and the logprob rounding logic in response/formatting.go. I intentionally included a small shim in sdk/js/openai_compat.ts to maintain the OpenAI-style event payload shape; that can be refactored if we prefer centralizing shape translation server-side.

Merge plan: squash-merge after approvals. Will monitor production streaming proxies for ~48 hours after rollout.

Marcus Li: Flow-control changes look reasonable; can you add a small doc blurb describing backpressure behavior so infra understands the proxy implications? (Added docs/ note in commit 4).
Hannah Kim: Found a flaky test on CI related to stream reconnects; was caused by a race in the test harness. Fixed by adding deterministic connection ordering in tests.

release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: improved streaming stability, role normalization, deterministic stop handling for streaming, streaming and final logprobs support, and structured response formatting helpers in SDKs.
